template_name: OECD Common Reporting Framework for AI Incidents (voluntary)
source_legislation: OECD, 'Towards a common reporting framework for AI incidents', OECD AI Papers No. 34 (Feb 2025), DSTI/DPC/GPAI(2024)5/FINAL, DOI 10.1787/f326d4ac-en

oecd_framework.source: OECD AI Papers No. 34 (Feb 2025); Box 2.2 selected-criteria counts; Table 2.2 mandatory asterisks; transcribed verbatim per RFC-0002 §5.7 / Appendix E Q2 — not invented.
oecd_framework.criterion_id_convention: oecd-crf-2025/<n> keyed to the OECD ordinal position (ACEF-local convention; OECD has no stable machine-readable criterion id scheme — RFC-0002 §5.5 / Appendix E Q2).
oecd_framework.non_binding_note: The OECD common reporting framework is a benchmark designed to serve BOTH mandatory and voluntary reporting; the 7 'mandatory' criteria are the framework's own completeness core, not a binding ACEF fail-gate. ACEF marks this template legal_force=voluntary: an unmet criterion surfaces as an advisory (warning) disposition, never a binding NOT_SATISFIED that blocks conformance. Distinct from the binding eu-ai-act-art73-2026 template.

mandatory_criteria.name: How is the AI system(s) related to the incident
mandatory_criteria.closed_value_set_note: Criterion #3's value set (OECD Annex C) is a closed enumeration that must be transcribed verbatim from the OECD source; that transcription is the v1.2 closed-enum surface (RFC-0002 §10 / Appendix C). In v1.1 #3 validates STRUCTURALLY only (criterion id + edition presence), never by enumerated value.

provisions.normative_text_ref: OECD CRF 2025, Table 2.2 (mandatory criteria, asterisked); Box 2.2 (selected-criteria counts)
provisions.description: The OECD common reporting framework designates SEVEN of its 29 criteria as mandatory (asterisked in Table 2.2): #1 Title, #2 Description of the incident, #3 How is the AI system(s) related to the incident, #4 Submitter information, #7 Supporting material(s), #10 Severity, #11 Harm type. These form the framework's completeness core. Because the OECD framework is a VOLUNTARY benchmark (legal_force=voluntary) — explicitly designed to serve both mandatory and voluntary reporting — ACEF surfaces an unmet mandatory criterion as an ADVISORY (warning) disposition, never a binding NOT_SATISFIED. The criteria live on incident_card.taxonomy_crosswalk.oecd.criteria[] (each id keyed to the OECD ordinal oecd-crf-2025/<n>, §5.5).

sub_provisions.description: How is the AI system(s) related to the incident (mandatory). Closed value set (Annex C) deferred to v1.2 — structural validation only in v1.1.

retention.basis: NOT ASSESSED. This profile has established no retention basis for the OECD common reporting framework for AI incidents (OECD AI Papers No. 34, February 2025) (OECD CRF 2025, Table 2.2 (mandatory criteria, asterisked); Box 2.2 (selected-criteria counts)). No retention determination has been made for this provision: the instrument was not assessed for records-retention duties and no period is asserted here. The OECD CRF is a reporting-taxonomy proposal with no legal force; any retention duty over incident records arises from the adopting jurisdiction's own instrument, not from the CRF. Absence of a figure is NOT a finding that no retention period applies: a retention duty may arise from this instrument, from an implementing instrument, or from generally applicable records law that this profile does not model. Establishing a cited basis requires a separate research pass against the primary text of the instrument.

provisions.evaluation_dsl_note: HONESTY (mirrors the eu-ai-act-art73-2026 template). The DSL-CORRECT check the generic engine CAN express is the existential presence + edition-pin of the OECD crosswalk member (exists_where on incident_card.taxonomy_crosswalk.oecd.edition). The PER-ORDINAL completeness check — 'does criteria[] contain an entry for each mandatory ordinal #1,2,3,4,7,10,11?' — is NOT DSL-expressible: criteria[] is an order-insensitive array (§5.10), exists_where resolves a SINGLE RFC-6901 pointer per record, and jsonpointer has NO array-wildcard, so no operator can scan array entries by an `id` predicate; hard-coding criteria/0/id would wrongly reject a valid card whose criteria are sorted differently (the index-0 anti-pattern). Encoding the 7 ordinals as fixed-index field_present rules is therefore a false signal and is NOT done. Instead: (a) the member-presence + edition-pin is encoded as an honest advisory exists_where rule; (b) the per-ordinal mandatory-core completeness is DECLARED in validator_delegated_enforcement and oecd_framework.mandatory_criteria for a richer (validator/SDK) completeness checker — and because the whole template is voluntary, even a delegated completeness gap is ADVISORY, never binding. All retained rules are warning severity.

validator_delegated_enforcement.why_not_dsl: criteria[] is an order-insensitive array; exists_where resolves one RFC-6901 pointer per record and jsonpointer has no array-wildcard, so the generic DSL cannot scan array entries by an `id` predicate or verify per-ordinal completeness without a brittle hard-coded index.

checks.requirement: incident_card.taxonomy_crosswalk.oecd.criteria[] contains an entry (keyed oecd-crf-2025/<n>) for each of the 7 mandatory ordinals #1, #2, #3, #4, #7, #10, #11. A missing mandatory criterion surfaces ADVISORY (warning / PARTIALLY_SATISFIED), never a binding NOT_SATISFIED — the OECD framework is voluntary.
checks.reason: Order-insensitive array-element scan by `id` predicate is not expressible in the generic ACEF DSL (no array-wildcard in jsonpointer; exists_where resolves a single pointer).

checks.requirement: OECD criterion #3 (oecd-crf-2025/3, 'How is the AI system(s) related to the incident' — Annex C value set) and criterion #19 (oecd-crf-2025/19, 'Incident linked to the functioning of critical functions/infrastructure' — CISA/EU critical-functions list) carry CLOSED value enumerations that must be transcribed VERBATIM from the OECD primary source before they can be enforced by value. That transcription is the v1.2 closed-enum surface (RFC-0002 §10 / Appendix C, residual caveat (b)). In v1.1 #3/#19 validate STRUCTURALLY only — presence of the criterion id and the edition pin (oecd-crf-2025) — never by enumerated value. The template MUST NOT invent OECD enum values.
checks.reason: The closed value sets for OECD #3 (Annex C) and #19 (critical-functions list) are external transcriptions scoped out of v1.1; inventing enum values would misrepresent the OECD source. v1.1 validates these members structurally (id/edition presence) only.

evaluation.message: ADVISORY (voluntary, never binding): an incident_card aligned to the OECD common reporting framework should carry a taxonomy_crosswalk.oecd member pinned to edition 'oecd-crf-2025'. This is the DSL-CORRECT existential presence check; the per-ordinal mandatory-core completeness (#1,2,3,4,7,10,11) is order-insensitive-array work delegated to the validator/SDK completeness checker (see validator_delegated_enforcement), and remains advisory. Covers OECD mandatory criteria oecd-crf-2025/1, oecd-crf-2025/2, oecd-crf-2025/3, oecd-crf-2025/4, oecd-crf-2025/7, oecd-crf-2025/10, oecd-crf-2025/11.

ADVISORY: an OECD-aligned incident_card should link to the subject AI system whose incident is reported (supports OECD criteria #8 Name/version and #9 Organisation enrichment); voluntary, non-binding.

provisions.normative_text_ref: OECD CRF 2025, Box 2.2 (selected criteria minus the 7 mandatory)
provisions.description: The remaining 22 of the 29 OECD criteria are OPTIONAL enrichment, provided 'where available' (OECD CRF 2025). They span the Date/Country/AI-system-name metadata (#5,6,8,9), the rest of Harm details (#12,13), People-and-planet (#14,15,16), Economic context (#17,18,19,20), Data/input (#21), AI model (#22,23,24), Task/output (#25,26), and Other information (#27,28,29). They are INFORMATIONAL in ACEF (info severity) — their absence is neither a fail nor a warning. Criterion #19 (critical-functions/infrastructure) carries a closed value set deferred to the v1.2 closed-enum surface (Appendix C); validated structurally only in v1.1.

provisions.evaluation_dsl_note: The 22 optional criteria are enrichment 'where available'; their per-ordinal presence is the same order-insensitive-array-scan the generic DSL cannot express. The single retained rule is an info-severity advisory that the OECD member exists at all; per-ordinal optional completeness is left to the validator/SDK and is purely informational (never warning, never fail).

evaluation.message: INFORMATIONAL: where available, an OECD-aligned incident_card may enrich with the 22 optional OECD criteria (#5,6,8,9,12-18,20-29). Their per-ordinal presence is delegated (order-insensitive array); criterion #19's closed critical-functions value set is deferred to the v1.2 closed-enum surface (Appendix C). Purely advisory, non-binding.
